summary: Enhance your skills in Monitoring and Evaluation for Economic Development Projects. Join our training course to drive impactful project outcomes and success.
lede: M&E for economic development projects provides a practical way to move beyond tracking expenditure, activities, and attendance to assess changes in employment, income, enterprise performance, market access, financial inclusion, and local economic resilience. You will learn to build a Theory of Change, logical framework, SMART indicators, baseline and target-setting approach, and evaluation matrix, using the OECD DAC criteria to examine relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, and sustainability. Practical work covers data quality assessment, sampling, outcome progress, and evidence reporting for management action, along with dashboards in Power BI or Microsoft Excel. You will also explore contribution analysis, outcome harvesting, quasi-experimental evaluation concepts, cost-effectiveness analysis, geospatial data considerations, and AI-assisted coding of qualitative evidence without needing advanced statistical modelling or machine-learning deployment.
audienceIntro: This M&E for Economic Development Projects course suits professionals responsible for planning, monitoring, evaluating, managing, financing, or communicating development interventions. It supports foundation-level learners who need a structured entry point and experienced practitioners who want to strengthen the consistency of their results systems.
modules: Theory of Change for Economic Development
prerequisites: You need access to a laptop for spreadsheet, dashboard, and digital data exercises. TrainingCred can provide sample economic development project datasets, templates, and exercise files. The course teaches KoboToolbox, Microsoft Excel, and Power BI at an operational application level, not at a software engineering or advanced statistical modelling level.
